label: North Atlantic Right Whale Population
delta: 23 calves in 2025–2026 season — best in 15 years
deltaNote: IUCN Critically Endangered. 23 calves confirmed in 2025–2026 season (Nov–Apr) — highest since 2009, first 15-year period with 20+ calves. ~70 reproductively active females. Trump administration backs H.R. 8509 to delay new rope regulations to 2035 (May 4, 2026), alarming conservation groups. Gear entanglement remains primary mortality driver.

label: Global Coral Reef Area Bleached — 4th Global Event
delta: Largest bleaching event ever recorded: Jan 2023 – Sep 2025
deltaNote: 4th global mass bleaching event impacted 84.4% of world reef area across 83 countries over 2.5 years. GBR: 73% of surveyed area bleached in 2024.

deltaNote: 145 countries have signed; 92 have ratified as of April 2026. Australia ratified March 2026 (88th party). CoP1 scheduled January 11–22, 2027. PrepCom 3 concluded April 2, 2026.

label: World's Coral Reefs Under Bleaching-Level Stress
contestNote: Percentage fluctuates with ocean temperatures; El Niño years see spikes above 80%. Cumulative impact of 4th global bleaching event reached 84.4% by Sep 2025.

label: Eastern Pacific Gray Whale Population
source: NOAA Fisheries Southwest Fisheries Science Center (NOAA-TM-NMFS-SWFSC-737, Jul 2026)
contestNote: NOAA's official 2025/2026 migration survey (95% CI: 15,930–20,530) puts the population back within its pre-2024 range, in tension with PEER/independent researchers' 'catastrophic mortality event' framing based on 145 stranding deaths. NOAA has not formally re-declared an Unusual Mortality Event.
deltaNote: NOAA published a new abundance estimate on July 15, 2026 based on visual, infrared-camera, and drone surveys off Granite Canyon, California, putting the population at ~17,750 — a rebound from the 2024/2025 estimate and comparable to levels during the 2019–2023 Unusual Mortality Event. The finding complicates (but does not resolve) the 'catastrophic mortality event' narrative from mid-2026's 145 recorded strandings from Mexico to Alaska. NOAA scientists caution that calf production has remained near record lows since 2019, and flagged migration-timing or methodology questions requiring further study.

label: Our Ocean Conference — Cumulative Commitments Since 2014
source: Our Ocean Conference / World Resources Institute (Jun 2026)
deltaNote: OOC11, the first Our Ocean Conference held in Africa, drew 5,000+ delegates from 100+ governments and organizations who announced 320 new commitments worth $6.4 billion — covering MPAs, fisheries transparency, coral reef resilience, and blue-economy investment. Since the series began in 2014, cumulative pledges now total over $176 billion across 3,200+ commitments, though implementation tracking of past promises remains contested.
